findings.issue: Repeatedly ran 'pkill -f node build' in the same bash chain, which terminated the agent's own shell (exit 143), forcing a retry turn each time — four occurrences without adapting.
findings.suggestion: Kill by port/PID (e.g. 'lsof -ti:3200 | xargs -r kill') or move cleanup out of the command chain so the shell survives.

findings.issue: API_BASE_URL is captured at module scope, so a value set after import wouldn't be picked up; the agent briefly worried about exactly this at turn 59 before finding the real (port-shadowing) cause.
findings.suggestion: Read process.env.API_BASE_URL lazily inside the fetch helper for robustness, though it works fine under adapter-node as used.

findings.issue: First curl of /pokemon/pikachu returned the not-found page (server presumably not ready or a transient miss) and was never root-caused, just re-probed successfully.
findings.suggestion: Wait for readiness (poll the health/200 endpoint) instead of an unslept first request; harmless here but the anomaly was left unexplained.

summary: An exemplary autonomous session: requirements, tests, design references and data shapes were exhaustively studied before coding, and implementation proceeded with almost no rework. The single 11-failure test run was diagnosed causally (the agent's own dev server shadowing the harness port) and fixed in one step, then verified with full clean-state reruns, flakiness checks, and screenshot-by-screenshot comparison against every design reference. The only recurring blemish is a pkill pattern that killed its own shell four times without adaptation.
